               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Wo unto thee Chorazin, wo unto thee Beth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />saida, for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ackcloth and ashes.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, then for you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And thou Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.21.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 13.20.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thess. 4.8.</ns0:note> He that heareth you, heareth me, and he that despiseth you, despiseth me: and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth,</ns0:hi> 10.40.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.<ns0:note place="bottom">As we before read of the Twelve coming back to give Christ an account of their success, so we here have the same of the Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venty; whether this Joy of the Seventy was more Carnal than it ought, they rather rejoycing in that new Power which they had received from Christ, than in the Demonstration of Christs Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Power, and the Confirmation of the Doctrine of the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel by these Miraculous Operations, is hard to determine; for tho Christs reply, seemeth to have a Check in it, yet it is so qualifyed by the Term <ns0:hi>Rather, v.</ns0:hi> 20. that we cannot from thence abso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lutely conclude any such thing from it. Here is a difference to be observed betwixt Christs and his Disciples casting out of Devils. Christ did it in <ns0:hi>his own Name,</ns0:hi> by his own Word of Command, Power and Authority; the Disciples did it in Christs Name, and by a Power, and Authority derived from him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as light<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning fall from heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Lightning comes suddenly, and with Thunder. The <ns0:hi>Thunder of the Gospel</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> brought down the Devil as <ns0:hi>Lightning,</ns0:hi> and in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed this is observable, the Devil is so busie in no places where the Gospel prevails, as in places where that joyful Sound is not come, whether we consider his Power with reference to Mens Bodies or Souls. This is one general advantage of Gospel Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, the Devil will not indure the sound of it, so as to impose upon Man-kind, at that rate which he doth upon ignorant Persons, that are Heathens, or only differing from them in that they are Baptized, and call themselves Christians. Christ <ns0:hi>saw this,</ns0:hi> as God, for the Devil is not visible to humane Senses, as neither are any Spirits, which shewed the impudence of that <ns0:hi>Popish Impostor in</ns0:hi> Germany, who selling Indulgences (by which he pretended Souls were delivered from <ns0:hi>Purgatory</ns0:hi>) called to the People to look up and see them fly away. But Christ could see it as God, for he cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly knew, that it would be, and that it already was the Blessed effect of the Gospel.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 16, 18.</ns0:note> I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.<ns0:note place="bottom">Christ doth here, 1. Confirm the Power before given to these Seventy for working Miracles, that they might not think, that it ceased upon the Determination of their first Mission, 2. He confirmeth his promise to them for his presence with them, and Protection of them. Interpreters think here is a manifest Allu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion to <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 91.13. <ns0:hi>Thou shalt tread upon the Lion, and Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der; the young Lyon, and Adder, thou shalt trample under thy Feet.</ns0:hi> Which must be understood Figuratively, the Sense being, that nothing should hurt them. This promise was more special<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly verifyed for some years, in Gods Protection of the first Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters of the Gospel, until they had done their Work, and shall be fulfilled in a Sense to the end of the World, according to the promise, in <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 91. Nothing shall hurt their Souls, as to the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour of God, and their Eternal Happiness, nor their Bodies so far forth as, or so long as God in his Wisdom shall judge fit. They have a further Power also given them more common to all the Ministers of the Gospel sent by Christ, yea, and to all Christians. They have a Power over <ns0:hi>all the Power of the Enemy,</ns0:hi> God will not be wanting to them in a Power to <ns0:hi>Resist the Devil,</ns0:hi> and they have a promise that being resisted, <ns0:hi>He shall Flee from them.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Notwithstanding in this rejoyce not, that the spirits are subject unto you, but rather rejoyce, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exo. 32.32. Isa. 4.3. Dan. 12.1. Phil. 4.3.</ns0:note> your names are written in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is an usual thing in Holy Writ, to have Prohibitions delive<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red in General Terms, which must be understood in a restrained Sense. That it is so here, appeareth plainly by the Word <ns0:hi>Rather,</ns0:hi> prefixed to <ns0:hi>Rejoyce,</ns0:hi> in the latter part of the Sentence. For it was doubtless a just cause of Joy, and Rejoycing to them that Christ had honoured them with such an extraordinary Gift and Power, but not of so <ns0:hi>much Ioy,</ns0:hi> as to know that their Names were <ns0:hi>Wrote in the Book of Life</ns0:hi>; for as the good was infinitely greater, so a proportionable Joy was requisite upon the assurance of it. The expression <ns0:hi>written in heaven,</ns0:hi> is equivalent to the be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:hi>Wrote in the Book of Life,</ns0:hi> whereby it signifyed, either the certain Designation of some to Eternal Life, or effectual cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling. We read of this Book of Life, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 3.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 20.12.15. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 27. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 22.19. it is called the Lambs Book, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 13.8. and it is said it was <ns0:hi>Written from the Foundation of the World,</ns0:hi> which will justify those Divines who understand it of a <ns0:hi>particu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lar Election from Eternity</ns0:hi>; whereas it is objected that when a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst the Twelve, there was a <ns0:hi>Son of Perdition,</ns0:hi> it is unrea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sonable to think that all the Seventy were elect Vessels. It is easily answered, that our Saviours Words were true according to the usual Phrase of speaking, if the Generality of them only were such. No<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> need our Saviour be understood as asserting, all their Names were so written, but only asserting the greatest cause of Joy to be, if Men can by their Calling find that their Election is sure. From our Saviours Words we may infe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, 1. That there is a <ns0:hi>Book of Life,</ns0:hi> an Election of Grace, 2. That there are <ns0:hi>Names written in this Book.</ns0:hi> It is an Election of Persons. 3. <ns0:hi>That Men may know that their Names are written in that Book,</ns0:hi> otherwise they could not rejoyce; no man rejoyceth, but in a good with which he hath some degree of Union. 4. That this is a greater cause of Joy, than for a Man to know that he hath a Power to cast out Devils. Men may be made use of to cast out Devils in Christs Name, who yet may go to the Devil at last, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.22. So cannot those whose <ns0:hi>Names are written in the Book of Life,</ns0:hi> but I cannot understand that our Saviour in these Words asserts that all the Names of the Seventy were wrote in that Book. The tendency of his discourse is rather to quicken them to give all dilligence to make sure of this cause of joy, and rejoycing.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:308" />21 In that hour Jesus rejoyced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father, for so it seemed good in thy sight.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 All things are delivered to me of my Father, and no <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 28.18. John 3.35.</ns0:note> man knoweth who the Son is, but the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and who the Father is, but the Son, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 6 44, 46.</ns0:note> and he to whom the Son will reveal <ns0:hi>him.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.29.27. where we met with these Words of our Saviour.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And he turned him unto <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> disciples, and said privately, ‖ Blessed <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the eyes which see the things that ye see.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 For I tell you, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Pet. 1.10.</ns0:note> many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard <ns0:hi>them.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 13.16, 17.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And he answering, said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 6.5.</ns0:note> Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 19.18.</ns0:note> thy neighbour as thy self.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 18.5. Ezek<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 20.11, 13.</ns0:note> thou shalt live.<ns0:note place="bottom">These four verses would incline one to think that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> here records the same piece of History, which we met with <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 22.35. and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 12.28. (See the Notes on both those Texts,) but neither of those Evangelists, have the following part of this discourse, which makes me doubtful whither <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> speaks of the same Person coming to Christ, which the others mention. A Lawyer he was, who came to our Saviour upon a design to <ns0:hi>Tempt,</ns0:hi> that is to make a trial of him, whither he would deliver any Doctrine contrary to the <ns0:hi>Law of Moses.</ns0:hi> It is plain that he fancy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed that the Eternal Life which Christ Preached, was to be obtained by doing what the Law required. Our Saviour agreeth it, that if he did what the Law required, according as he himself had given an account of it, <ns0:hi>h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> should Live.</ns0:hi> I apprehend no absurdity, to affirm that our Saviour speaks here of living Eternally. It is rather absurd to fancy, that our Saviour did not answer <ns0:hi>ad idem,</ns0:hi> to the thing about which the questions was propounded. Neither is Salvation impossible, because the Law in it self could not give Life, but because of <ns0:hi>the weakness of our Flesh,</ns0:hi> so as we cannot fulfil it. So that considering our infirmity, the Law serveth to us only as a <ns0:hi>Schoolmaster,</ns0:hi> to bring us to Christ, and as a <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> which we ought to shoot at, tho we cannot shoot home, a rule to direct us in our duty, tho we cannot perform or fulfil it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 But he willing to justifie himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?<ns0:note place="bottom">This Lawyers desire to justifie himself, spake him an Hypocrite. The reason of that Question <ns0:hi>who is my Neighbour,</ns0:hi> was the notion of the <ns0:hi>Neighbour,</ns0:hi> (mentioned in the Law) which the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> had, who counted none their <ns0:hi>Neighbours,</ns0:hi> but their Friends, and <ns0:hi>benefactors,</ns0:hi> at least none but those that were of their own Nation or particular Sect, and had taught their People, that they might hate their Enemies. Our Saviour (this being but a captious question considering the received Interpretation amongst them of the Law of God,) doth not think fit to answer his questi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on directly, but telling him a story, maketh him answer him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And Jesus answering, said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and departed, leaving <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> half-dead.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And by chance there came down a certain priest that way, and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked <ns0:hi>on him,</ns0:hi> and passed by on the other side.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 But a certain Samaritane, as he journeyed, came where he was, and when he saw him, he had com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />passion <ns0:hi>on him.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oyl and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And on the morrow when he departed, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See on</ns0:hi> Math. 20.2.</ns0:note> he took out two pence, and gave <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And he said, He that shewed mercy on him, Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou like<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is certain that the <ns0:hi>Principal Scope</ns0:hi> of our Saviour in this History, or <ns0:hi>Parable,</ns0:hi> was to convince the <ns0:hi>Lawyer, that everyone is our Neighbour, to whom God offered us an opportunity of doing good,</ns0:hi> whether he be of our Nation, or Religion yea or no. Every object of our Mercy is our <ns0:hi>Neighbour,</ns0:hi> whom God requireth us to love as our selves, this was quite contrary to the common Doctrine of the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> Interpreting the Law, <ns0:hi>Thou shalt love thy Neighbour as thy self,</ns0:hi> and excellently served our Saviours design, to shew this Lawyer that he understood not, much less observed the Law of God in that manner, as that he could justify himself from the <ns0:hi>Violation</ns0:hi> of it. He also by the by sheweth him, that the <ns0:hi>Samaritanes,</ns0:hi> whom the Jews so much abhorred, better understood the Law of God, then the <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical Guides</ns0:hi> of those times, who yet pretend to be teachers of it to others, for some of them by the light of Nature discerned themselves obliged, to do good to every one that stood in need of their help, or if not by the <ns0:hi>light of Nature,</ns0:hi> yet by the light of <ns0:hi>Revelation in the Law of Moses,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> by their false Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pretation of the <ns0:hi>Divine Law,</ns0:hi> had taught People to omit a great part of their Duty, required by the Divine Law, and so could not hope to be justified or to obtain eternal Life, and Salvation from the observation of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entred into a certain village: and a certain woman named <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 12.2, 3.</ns0:note> Martha, received him into her house.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And she had a sister called Mary, which also <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 22.3.</ns0:note> sat at Jesus feet, and heard his word.<ns0:note place="bottom">Interpreters think this Village was <ns0:hi>Bethany,</ns0:hi> and that this <ns0:hi>Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tha</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mary,</ns0:hi> were the same which are mentioned <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 11.2. Inns probably were not so frequent then, and in those places, as they are now, so as strangers were often received in private houses. Christ looseth no opportunity of Preaching the Gospel, while they were preparing Supper, he was entertaining the Family with the glad tidings of the Gospel, <ns0:hi>the feast made upon the Mountain of fat things, Isaiah</ns0:hi> 25.6.) The Lips of the righteous feed many. It was their fashion to have Disciples sit at their Doctors Feet, to hear their Word, there <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> fixeth her self.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 But Martha was cumbred about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.<ns0:note place="bottom">Two things are blameable in <ns0:hi>Martha.</ns0:hi> 1. That she made two much ado about the entertainment of our Saviour, that she enter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained our Saviour, she did well, but herein she erred, that she made her entertainment of him so troublesome, as it would not give her leave to take that advantage, which she might, or ought to have done from the entertainment of a Prophet. 2. That she is displeased with her Sister, because she would not lend her her hand, but chose rather to sit at Christs Feet, and hear his Word, and desireth Christ to send her away to her assistance.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And Jesus answered, and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and troubled about many things.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 27.4.</ns0:note> But one thing is needful. And Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour plainly blameth <ns0:hi>Martha,</ns0:hi> for her too great sollici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude, and trouble to provide a Dinner, or Supper for him, who had Meat to eat which she was not aware of, it being his Meat and Drink to do the Will of his Father, and to Preach the Gospel. Interpreters much trouble themselves, in determining what that <ns0:hi>one thing</ns0:hi> is, which our Saviour here saith is needful. Some think our Saviour meaneth no more then <ns0:hi>one dish is enough,</ns0:hi> but this certain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly is too low a sense. Others would have this <ns0:hi>one thing,</ns0:hi> to be a Life of <ns0:hi>Meditation and Contemplation,</ns0:hi> and that this was that <ns0:hi>good part Mary had chosen.</ns0:hi> If <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> had thus spent her whole Life, they might have said something for this. But certainly <ns0:hi>Marys</ns0:hi> chusing to take advantage of Christs company, rather to spend an hour or two in hearing of him, then in preparing a Supper for him, will prove no such thing. I should Interprete it <ns0:hi>gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally,</ns0:hi> concerning <ns0:hi>the care of the Soul with reference to eternity.</ns0:hi> That is certainly the <ns0:hi>one thing necessary,</ns0:hi> that was the <ns0:hi>better part,</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> had chosen, as to which Christ would not discourage her, nor any way blunt the edge of those holy desires, he had kindled in her, an effect of which study and care, was her sitting at the Feet of Christ, to hear his Word.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
